quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for what follows.
quests.explanation: Basis (Given that renewable capacity keeps expanding) + main clause (coal plants are closing faster than expected). 'Given that' presents a fact as already established, then builds a conclusion on top of it.
quests.textToSpeak: Given that renewable capacity keeps expanding, coal plants are closing faster than expected.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Were it not for' is a formal inversion meaning 'if it were not for'.
quests.explanation: Hypothetical negation (Were it not for early whistleblowers) + result (the data breach might never have come to light). 'Were it not for + noun' imagines the absence of something important and its consequence.
quests.textToSpeak: Were it not for early whistleblowers, the data breach might never have come to light.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Should' at the start is a formal substitute for 'if...should'.
quests.explanation: Condition (Should symptoms persist beyond a week despite rest) + result (doctors generally recommend further testing). Starting with 'Should' is a formal way to express 'if this happens', common in official guidance.
quests.textToSpeak: Should symptoms persist beyond a week despite rest, doctors generally recommend further testing.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'However + adjective' at the start sets up a strong contrast with what follows.
quests.explanation: Concession (However promising the pilot program looked) + main clause (funding ran out within a year). 'However + adjective + subject + verb' concedes a strong point before contradicting it.
quests.textToSpeak: However promising the pilot program looked, funding ran out within a year.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'For all its X' means 'despite having many X' — a compact concession.
quests.explanation: Concession (For all its flaws) + main clause (the festival remains the city's most beloved tradition). 'For all its + noun' packs a whole concession into just a few words.
quests.textToSpeak: For all its flaws, the festival remains the city's most beloved tradition.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Much of what...' turns an entire idea into the grammatical subject.
quests.explanation: Subject (Much of what scientists once considered permanently stable) + is now shifting (verb) + with surprising speed (manner). This structure nominalizes a whole belief to comment on how it has changed.
quests.textToSpeak: Much of what scientists once considered permanently stable is now shifting with surprising speed.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'No sooner had X than Y' shows two events happening in extremely quick succession.
quests.explanation: First event (No sooner had the app launched) + second event (than millions of users signed up). This dramatic inversion emphasizes how immediately the second event followed the first.
quests.textToSpeak: No sooner had the app launched than millions of users signed up.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Nowhere is this more evident than in X' points to the clearest example.
quests.explanation: Claim (Nowhere is this more evident) + than in the rise of telemedicine visits (the clearest example). This inverted structure often introduces the strongest piece of supporting evidence.
quests.textToSpeak: Nowhere is this more evident than in the rise of telemedicine visits.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'As + noun + continues to + verb' frames an ongoing trend as background.
quests.explanation: Background trend (As streaming continues to reshape entertainment) + main clause (cinemas are fighting to stay relevant). 'As...continues to' frames one change as the backdrop for another.
quests.textToSpeak: As streaming continues to reshape entertainment, cinemas are fighting to stay relevant.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'It is precisely because X that Y' emphasizes the exact cause of something.
quests.explanation: Emphasized cause (It is precisely because the exam is difficult) + result (that it carries so much weight). This cleft-like structure singles out one cause as the true reason behind an effect.
quests.textToSpeak: It is precisely because the exam is difficult that it carries so much weight.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'So + adjective + that' links an extreme degree to its direct consequence.
quests.explanation: Cause (The heatwave was so severe) + result (that entire crops failed within days). 'So...that' is a classic pattern connecting an intense quality to its dramatic outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: The heatwave was so severe that entire crops failed within days.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Not until X did Y' delays the main action until a specific point.
quests.explanation: Delay (Not until the outage crossed six hours) + inverted action (did engineers escalate the alert). 'Not until' at the start triggers inversion and emphasizes how long the delay lasted.
quests.textToSpeak: Not until the outage crossed six hours did engineers escalate the alert.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Such was the X that Y' is a formal way to show an extreme degree led to an action.
quests.explanation: Degree (Such was the demand for appointments) + result (that the clinic doubled its staff). A more formal, dramatic version of 'The demand was so great that...'.
quests.textToSpeak: Such was the demand for appointments that the clinic doubled its staff.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Behind X lies Y' reveals something hidden beneath a visible surface.
quests.explanation: Visible thing (Behind every award-winning film) + hidden reality (lies months of exhausting work) + that rarely gets any recognition (relative clause modifying 'work'). 'Behind X lies Y' vividly contrasts appearance with underlying reality, and the added relative clause reinforces just how invisible that effort usually is.
quests.textToSpeak: Behind every award-winning film lies months of exhausting work that rarely gets any recognition.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'If anything' suggests the opposite of a doubt, reinforcing a point.
quests.explanation: Reinforcement (If anything) + claim (the new grading system has made expectations even clearer). 'If anything' strengthens a statement, especially against an assumption it might be false.
quests.textToSpeak: If anything, the new grading system has made expectations even clearer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'More often than not' means 'usually', placed for emphasis at the start.
quests.explanation: Frequency phrase (More often than not) + main clause (small local changes add up to significant results). A slightly more vivid alternative to 'usually' or 'generally'.
quests.textToSpeak: More often than not, small local changes add up to significant results.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'What began as X has become Y' traces a transformation from start to now.
quests.explanation: Origin (What began as a simple messaging app) + present state (has become an essential utility). This cleft-like structure highlights the distance between where something started and ended up.
quests.textToSpeak: What began as a simple messaging app has become an essential utility.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Underlying X is the assumption that Y' exposes a hidden belief.
quests.explanation: Visible thing (Underlying every public health campaign) + hidden belief (is the assumption that people will listen). Useful for questioning assumptions that are rarely stated directly.
quests.textToSpeak: Underlying every public health campaign is the assumption that people will listen.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'To the extent that' sets a careful limit on how strong a claim really is.
quests.explanation: Limiting clause (To the extent that motivation can be taught) + main clause (this program comes remarkably close). This phrase carefully qualifies a claim instead of stating it as an absolute.
quests.textToSpeak: To the extent that motivation can be taught, this program comes remarkably close.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Time and again' emphasizes that a pattern has repeated many times.
quests.explanation: Repetition phrase (Time and again) + main clause (independent musicians have outpaced major labels across every streaming platform). A vivid way of saying 'repeatedly' or 'many times over'.
quests.textToSpeak: Time and again, independent musicians have outpaced major labels across every streaming platform.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: This structure gently warns against a common but flawed assumption.
quests.explanation: Warning (It would be a mistake to assume that) + flawed belief (recycling alone can solve the crisis). A diplomatic way to correct a common misconception without sounding harsh.
quests.textToSpeak: It would be a mistake to assume that recycling alone can solve the crisis.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Seldom has' combines a negative adverb with present perfect for dramatic effect.
quests.explanation: Seldom has a single device changed (inverted present perfect) + daily habits as quickly and as completely as this one (rest). A formal, emphatic way of saying 'this rarely, if ever, happens'.
quests.textToSpeak: Seldom has a single device changed daily habits as quickly and as completely as this one.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Whatever the reason' sets aside the cause to focus on the fact itself.
quests.explanation: Dismissal of cause (Whatever the reason) + main clause (hospital wait times keep growing across the country). Lets the writer state a fact without needing to explain why.
quests.textToSpeak: Whatever the reason, hospital wait times keep growing across the country.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'On closer inspection' signals a first impression that didn't hold up.
quests.explanation: Signal phrase (On closer inspection) + revised conclusion (the survey's impressive results turned out to be misleading). Common when a deeper look changes the original conclusion.
quests.textToSpeak: On closer inspection, the survey's impressive results turned out to be misleading.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Far from + verb-ing' rules out an expected outcome before stating the truth.
quests.explanation: Rejected expectation (Far from fading away) + actual reality (vinyl records have found an entirely new audience). 'Far from' emphatically denies an assumption before replacing it.
quests.textToSpeak: Far from fading away, vinyl records have found an entirely new audience.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'In many respects' softens a broad claim by acknowledging some limits.
quests.explanation: Qualifying phrase (In many respects) + main clause (the policy succeeded exactly as its designers intended). Signals a generally true claim without insisting it's true in every way.
quests.textToSpeak: In many respects, the policy succeeded exactly as its designers intended.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Whether or not' shows the outcome doesn't depend on which possibility is true.
quests.explanation: Irrelevant condition (Whether or not the rumors are true) + main clause (the announcement rattled investors). Shows the result held regardless of which possibility was correct.
quests.textToSpeak: Whether or not the rumors are true, the announcement rattled investors.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'As if to prove the point' frames an event as perfectly, almost suspiciously timed.
quests.explanation: Framing phrase (As if to prove the point) + main clause (hospital readmissions dropped the following month). Adds a touch of narrative irony to a real, factual outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: As if to prove the point, hospital readmissions dropped the following month.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'All too often' expresses frustration that something happens more than it should.
quests.explanation: Frustration phrase (All too often) + main clause (talented students are overlooked simply for being quiet). Stronger than 'often' — it implies the frequency is a real problem.
quests.textToSpeak: All too often, talented students are overlooked simply for being quiet.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'By the time X, Y had already happened' shows one event overtaking another.
quests.explanation: Reference point (By the time the treaty was signed) + earlier completed event (three species had already vanished). Past perfect shows the extinction happened before the signing.
quests.textToSpeak: By the time the treaty was signed, three species had already vanished.
